note: Hand-drafted first patches from Books I and II, so the Mirror can be populated without an API key. Quotes are from the George Long translation; the Steward flags any quote it cannot find verbatim once the corpus is downloaded.

patches.quote: From my grandfather Verus I learned good morals and the government of my temper.
patches.rationale: Marcus credits his grandfather with his moral grounding and his control of temper.

patches.quote: From the reputation and remembrance of my father, modesty and a manly character.
patches.rationale: His father, known to him mostly by memory and reputation, models modesty.

patches.quote: From my mother, piety and beneficence, and abstinence, not only from evil deeds, but even from evil thoughts; and further, simplicity in my way of living, far removed from the habits of the rich.
patches.rationale: His mother teaches piety, generosity, purity of thought and a simple life that rejects the habits of the rich.

patches.quote: From Rusticus I received the impression that my character required improvement and discipline
patches.rationale: Rusticus awakens his sense that his character needs work, the root of his practice of self-improvement.

patches.quote: From Apollonius I learned freedom of will and undeviating steadiness of purpose; and to look to nothing else, not even for a moment, except to reason
patches.rationale: Apollonius ties steadiness of purpose to looking only to reason: attending to reason keeps the will steady.

causal_edges.mechanism: looking to nothing but reason keeps the will from wavering

patches.quote: Begin the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busy-body, the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial.
patches.rationale: Expecting difficult people each morning is a practice meant to blunt vexation before it arises.

causal_edges.mechanism: an expected offence does not take him by surprise

patches.quote: To act against one another then is contrary to nature; and it is acting against one another to be vexed and to turn away.
patches.rationale: Vexation is itself a way of acting against others, so it undermines cooperation and breaks with nature.

causal_edges.mechanism: to be vexed and turn away is to act against one another
we are made for co-operation, so working together is acting by nature

patches.quote: for we are made for co-operation, like feet, like hands, like eyelids, like the rows of the upper and lower teeth.
patches.rationale: People belong together like parts of one body; cooperation is part of human nature.

patches.quote: Every moment think steadily as a Roman and a man to do what thou hast in hand with perfect and simple dignity
patches.rationale: Steady attention to the task at hand is how dignity is carried out moment to moment.

causal_edges.mechanism: a steady will can think steadily every moment
doing what is in hand, simply and fully, is dignity in practice
